fit_contract.optimizer: five-start screen with 30 AdamW plus up to 60 strong-Wolfe L-BFGS iterations; then deep L-BFGS polish of the selected solution until projected KKT <=1e-5 or a preflight-corrected maximum of five 200-iteration polish blocks
fit_contract.preflight_amendment: Before inspecting predictive performance, the first fold exposed an optimizer-state bug: the deep-polish restart reconstructed the centered station effect instead of preserving the selected raw station vector, and stalled at 1.3e-5 after five blocks. Preserving the exact selected raw vector reached 8.84e-6 in the first polish block. Subsequent engineering-only monitoring found that rare folds can stop with only the physical v_f gradient at 1.3e-5 to 1.7e-5 because the raw sigmoid gradient and function change are already tiny. Such folds receive a bounded one-dimensional physical-scale v_f minimization followed by one final joint L-BFGS polish; R037 and R105 verified KKT values of 9.31e-6 and 6.34e-6. Once this rescue was verified without inspecting predictions, the trigger was moved immediately after any polish block for which v_f is the sole remaining KKT violation, rather than wasting all five identical-condition blocks. Engineering-only replay of R033 then showed that v_f correction can expose a different physical-process coordinate as the sole residual violation. Before inspecting predictions, the rescue was therefore generalized to at most eight deterministic Gauss-Seidel bounded one-dimensional minimizations of the currently largest physical-process KKT residual, with joint L-BFGS used only when the remaining violation lies in the station or gamma block. The terminal-tree stress fold T020 further showed joint Hessian scale competition across the gamma/site and process blocks. For such rare unresolved folds, up to eight deterministic alternating rounds optimize gamma plus site residuals conditionally on a cached fixed-process prediction, then optimize process parameters conditionally on the fitted head, followed when needed by the same exact physical-coordinate correction. If a process update leaves the final gamma gradient above tolerance, a final head-ending Gauss-Seidel sweep of at most 24 cached head fits and exact physical-coordinate corrections is allowed; a deterministic 1,000-step low-rate Adam bridge is used only when the cached conditional head itself fails the unchanged gradient gate before its final L-BFGS. If related process coordinates still cycle, at most six final block rounds use exact-gradient bounded L-BFGS-B on the eight-dimensional physical process vector followed by the same cached conditional head fit. The cached head losses omit only process-only constants and therefore have exactly the same gamma/site gradient as the registered objective; the physical L-BFGS-B gradient is obtained from the registered raw-parameter autograd gradient by the exact sigmoid Jacobian. Failure to meet the unchanged 1e-5 gate still aborts the worker. The model equation, objective, bounds, starts, initialization, likelihood and gate were not changed; every rescue round and corrected coordinate is recorded per fold.
fit_contract.resource_amendment: The host exposes 32 logical processors. Before any aggregate predictive result was inspected, profiling compared safe checkpoint layouts. Four two-thread workers underused the host; fourteen single-thread workers stayed below 28 GiB but required about 25 minutes per fold. The validated two-thread preflight required about 8-10 minutes per fold, so the formal layout is eight two-thread workers (at most 16 threads, 50% of logical processors). Nine valid KKT-passing folds produced by the single-thread engineering probe are reused; one 1.3e-5 fold is automatically rejected and recomputed, while incomplete work is discarded through fold-atomic writes. When two failed shard-front folds left all remaining work concentrated in only two shards, an engineering-only fold-id mode was added before aggregate predictions were inspected. It uses the identical fit function and writes one independent atomic checkpoint triplet per requested fold, allowing up to eight two-thread workers to recover the remaining registered folds without changing fold membership, preprocessing, initialization, objective, predictions or gates.
